lead: 3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ — buying the invasion scare, three times over
smaller: Aerospace & Defense ETF / ITA — buying the arsenal and the target
Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — the glitchy launch starts to cost
Wheat / ZW=F — the breadbasket war premium
why_lead: Eve-of-invasion buy-the-dip faith, expressed through the triple-leveraged Nasdaq 100 fund. Significant own-card move: TQQQ 45.14 USD, -7.65% 1-session and -21.22% 5-session, against S&P 500 4,225.50 (-1.84% / -5.49%), Nasdaq 100 13,509.43 (-2.60% / -7.60%), VIX 31.02 (+2.21 pts) and Robinhood -20.56% over five sessions (prior close 2022-02-23). Chronology: material update and promotion of the 2022-02-22 secondary item '3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ — the YOLO dip-buy with triple leverage' (TQQQ then 50.44 USD on the 18 February close, before the correction was confirmed). Changed catalyst: the S&P 500 confirmed a correction on war fears (n1901) and fell a further 1.84%, Ukraine declared a state of emergency with the ruble and Russian bonds hammered (n1281), satellite photos showed a build-up (n1282) and the separatists asked Putin for military help (n1278). Changed attention, all published after the 22 February cutoff: MarketWatch's first-correction-in-two-years 'what history says' piece and bullish-divergence signal (n1908, n1909), Business Insider's Mahaney buy list (n1719), Kiplinger's conflict-and-your-investments guide (n1570), Time's meme-stock lessons (n0541), NYT on correction-plus-sanctions (n0640), MarketWatch on Fed speed (n1850). The 22 February item's evidence (Yahoo YOLO piece, Fortune 'how low', A Wealth of Common Sense crash recovery, AdvisorHub leveraged-ETF charge, 'peak stupid') is deliberately not re-cited. Split view: Raymond James (n0445) and MarketWatch's divergence vs Wall St banks' recession fears (n0093), Fed speed (n1850) and the March hike with 50 bps calls (n1801); options expiration (n1571) as positioning risk. Invasion is treated only as a pending risk.
why_smaller: Aerospace & Defense ETF / ITA: material update of the 2022-02-22 secondary item 'Lockheed Martin / LMT — the war trade finally gets its trigger'. New evidence published 22–23 February: the FT reports ETF investors piling into Russian equities and defence stocks (n0837), which adds the Russia 'buy the target' leg: markets pared a plunge (n1245), Sberbank/VTB rebounded after escaping UK sanctions (n0632), ruble/bonds hit (n1281), Buffett avoids Russia (n0658). New card evidence for the defence leg: LMT 388.90 USD +0.70% / +1.75% 5-session, GD +1.64% 5-session vs S&P -5.49%, while ITA fell 1.14% to 101.69 USD (-3.98% 5-session) and RTX/NOC fell.

Digital World Acquisition / DWAC: carryover of the 2022-02-21 and 2022-02-22 leads, deliberately demoted to a secondary item. Material update with evidence published after the 22 February cutoff: the reopening surge (n0648), Apptopia's 170k downloads (n1569), the 13-hour crash (n1574), the Washington Post's 'disastrous launch' verdict (n1595) and an EU legal hurdle (n1596); card shows the first post-launch red day, 88.50 USD -4.74% 1-session but +9.06% 5-session and +28.30% 20-session. The waitlist, Nunes end-of-March, Hannity/Greene and logo-dispute headlines used on 21–22 February are not re-cited, and the hook was changed from the waitlist to the cost of the glitches.

Wheat / ZW=F: a distinct food-inflation war-premium narrative and the day's biggest commodity move after TTF gas: 876.00 US cents/bu, +3.76% 1-session, +12.34% 5-session, corn +7.17% and soybeans +7.98% 5-session (prior close 2022-02-23), with CNBC's breadbasket explainer (n1703), Reuters on curbed food supplies (n0571), Successful Farming's Wednesday close (n1714) and Bloomberg's fertilizer warning with Mosaic +2.29% (n0715). No earlier retail item covered grains.
considered_not_chosen: Gold / GC=F and GDX vs bitcoin (CNBC 'digital gold is falling apart', n0848; gold 1,910.40 USD/oz +2.92% 5-session, GDX +6.93%, BTC 37,296.57 USD -6.83% 5-session): dropped because 2022-02-21 already ran both Bitcoin 'digital gold flunks the weekend war test' and GDX 'the old haven still earns its keep', and 2022-02-14 ran GDX as the invasion hedge; one new CNBC headline did not justify a third consecutive version.

ARK Innovation ETF / ARKK (60.88 USD, -19.13% 5-session; Cathie Wood 'way undervalued' n1516, misallocation n1532): the same Cathie Wood headlines carried the 2022-02-21 ARKK item; folded the dip-buying family into the TQQQ lead instead.

Ford Motor / F EV-split story: ran as a 2022-02-22 smaller item; Ford's CEO has since said there are no plans to spin off the EV business (Reuters n0976), but no retail-attention evidence or card catalyst justified revisiting it.

Block / SQ and Coinbase Global / COIN into results (SQ 88.72 USD -22.99% 5-session, Investopedia preview n0685; COIN 172.74 USD -17.33% 5-session): pending results only, no outcome eligible; a preview cannot carry a crowd story.

Lucid Group / LCID (23.97 USD, -6.04% 1-session, -32.40% 20-session): results were due after the 23 February close and no eligible headline establishes the outcome; recall items (n0669, n1709) too thin.
Vertiv / VRT (-36.74% 1-session) and Airbnb / ABNB (-9.20%): large moves without a crowd narrative; HIMS (+13.10%) and DraftKings (+5.59%) without an explaining own-date headline.
Oil ETFs / USO (Seeking Alpha top oil ETFs n1150, NPR $100 oil n1242): Brent was flat on the session (+0.00%), so wheat was the cleaner commodity war-premium story.

Avoided as possibly after the cutoff: n0135 (Reuters 'Expert views on Russian forces invading Ukraine', stamped 23 February but describing the invasion), n1265 (excluded), n0753 (NYT 'Russia-Ukraine crisis shakes markets, but long-term outlook is better', publication time uncertain). Reuters LIVE MARKETS blog posts (n0733 '2018', n1053, n1109) rejected as live-blog items.
